data.body: METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION - reliability figures are CEILINGS, not unmeasurable. An earlier framing this session called CE's reliability unobservable from its artifacts, because the skill's inline fallback masks persona losses. That was wrong and discarded usable information. The error in this census is one-sided toward flattery: masked substitution, retries that overwrite failures, and failures known only because an orchestrator volunteered them can each only make an arm look BETTER than it is, never worse. None can manufacture a failure that did not occur. Therefore an observed reliability figure is an UPPER BOUND, with true reliability at or below it - a usable result rather than an absence of one. What this study bought is a TIGHTER ceiling than artifacts alone give: suppressing the inline fallback by instruction, and preserving failed attempts in superseded/ and runs/replicates/ rather than letting retries overwrite them, pushes the bound down toward the true rate. A reader of CE artifacts alone would infer a ceiling near one hundred percent; this study's is markedly lower. One counter-directional error is recorded so the bound is not claimed cleaner than it is: premature loss declarations inflate observed failure, and two recorded persona losses were provably wrong because the persona returned seconds later. Masking dominates, but the CE persona figure carries error in both directions, which is why losses are graded against explicit criteria rather than pooled. This framing applies to every arm, not just CE: mini's twenty Submitted runs, rebar's recovered web-search aborts, and superpowers' inline-vs-dispatched runs are all ceilings on their respective reliabilities.
